newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-German economic recovery only moderate - Ifo.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-German economic recovery only moderate - Ifo.

text.p: Karl-Heinz Oppenlaender, president of Germany's Ifo economic research institute, said on Friday that a mild improvement in Germany's business climate in June showed the economic recovery was progressing but only very moderately.
West Germany's business climate improved for a third month in June, with the Ifo index rising to 96.0 from a revised 95.4 in May -- above market expectations.
Analysts said the index's gain reflected the influence of a weaker mark, which was boosting profits and sentiment in the export sector.
"The improvement of the business situation reflects a better profit situation." said Gernot Nerb, economist at Salomon Brothers in Frankfurt. "The weak mark and higher export profits are reflected."
The German currency, which touched its lowest point for almost six years earlier this week at around 1.8040 to the dollar, was trading at 1.7949 to the dollar by 1300 GMT.
A softer mark against other foreign currencies increases demand abroad for exported German goods, since their prices are pushed lower by exchange rate differences.
But Ifo's Oppenlaender, speaking to Reuters in Munich after the data were released, said the index showed that "the economic recovery is progressing further, but in a very moderate way."
He also said it was important to note that despite a rise in the climate index -- which reflects firms' assessments of current conditions -- the index for business expectations dropped back.
Ifo's west German business expectations index eased to 103.7 in June from 104.1 in May, while expectations in the east were barely changed, reading 87.8 in June down from 87.9 previously.

"We are currently in a situation in which expectations should be improving," Oppenlaender said, adding that such an improvement could only come about when investors and firms became more confident about the future business environment.
Instead, Oppenlaender said, uncertainty in business circles and among investors was becoming more grave.
Oppenlaender said the east German climate index, which inched back to 103.6 from an upward revised 103.7 in May, showed economic progress there was still faltering.

Matthias Haffner, economist at BZW in Frankfurt, also said the numbers were not encouraging. "The east German figure shows construction in the east is still not so good. In spite of the dollar rise, the expectations in west Germany are not so good," he said.

But analysts at UBS in Frankfurt said any continuance of mark weakness could help the German economic environment in the coming months and may even begin to filter through to Germany's floundering labour market.

"If ... the mark remains weak, leading to further improvements in export prospects, then this constellation might eventually lead to a significant upward revision in production plans and a turn in the labour market in the quarters ahead," they said in a commentary on the Ifo numbers.
